form_analysis.feedback: Masterful general aftercare template for chemical peels. Establishes universal, critical principles: vigilant sun protection, strict moisturization, and absolute avoidance of picking. Perfectly sets the stage for more specific peel instructions. Includes clear emergency symptom recognition.

form_data.introduction: This document outlines the UNIVERSAL aftercare principles for chemical peel recovery. Adhering to these instructions is NON-NEGOTIABLE for proper healing, to achieve optimal results, and to minimise risks of complications, including scarring and pigment changes.

instructions.general_directive: Follow these instructions precisely. Your peel aftercare is as important as the peel itself.

sections.title: The Healing Timeline (General Guide)
sections.content: Day 1-2: Redness, tightness, swelling. Day 2-5: Darkening, frosting (if applicable), followed by peeling/flaking. Day 5-7: Peeling completes, reveals pink, new skin. Day 7-14: Pinkness fades, hyperpigmentation may surface. Day 14+: Full results visible as skin matures. *Timeline varies by peel depth.*

sections.title: The Cardinal Rules
items: 1. SUN PROTECTION IS MANDATORY: New skin is extremely vulnerable. Avoid all direct sun. Apply a physical/mineral sunscreen (SPF 30-50) every 90 minutes if outdoors. Wear a wide-brimmed hat.

2. MOISTURIZE CONSTANTLY: Keep the skin lubricated with the provided/approved ointment or moisturizer. Peeling skin that is dry will crack, itch, and heal poorly. 'Slugging' (applying a thick occlusive) at night may be recommended.
3. DO NOT PICK OR PULL: Let the skin shed NATURALLY. Forcing peel can cause bleeding, scarring, infection, and permanent dyspigmentation.
4. USE ONLY APPROVED PRODUCTS: Do not introduce any new active ingredients (retinoids, acids, Vitamin C) until cleared by your provider.

sections.title: Cleansing
sections.content: Cleanse only with a gentle, non-exfoliating wash as directed, using fingertips only. Pat dry, do not rub. You may be advised to use a diluted vinegar rinse for certain peels.

sections.title: Managing Discomfort
sections.content: Cool compresses can soothe burning/stinging. Sleep on your back with head elevated to reduce swelling. Over-the-counter pain relief (like acetaminophen) can be used if needed. Itching is common during peeling; an oral antihistamine may help.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions
items: No exercise, sweating, saunas, steam, or hot showers until peeling is complete and skin is no longer open or raw.
Avoid swimming (pools, ocean) until skin is fully healed (at least 1 week).

sections.title: Infection and Complication Awareness
sections.content: Contact your provider IMMEDIATELY if you experience: Severe pain not relieved by cool compresses, signs of infection (yellow/green pus, increasing redness/warmth, fever), cold sore outbreak, or the development of large, painful blisters.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: Do not apply makeup until the initial peeling phase is completely finished (usually 5-7 days). Applying makeup over peeling skin can cause clumping and introduce bacteria.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Expect redness and sensitivity for several weeks with deeper peels.
Hyperpigmentation (darkening) can occur post-peel, especially with sun exposure. This is why SPF is critical.
Final results are assessed at 4-6 weeks post-peel. Multiple peels are often needed for significant concerns.
